summary: Gramsci and McKay. edge_844.relationship: The liberal order framework is Gramscian: liberal order as hegemony and the national-political 'commonsense' (2000)
edge_844.evidence_note: McKay's abstract (2000) maps Canada as 'a project of liberal rule in northern North America' through which 'liberal order became the national-political ‘commonsense’'. Ajzenstat (2009) describes McKay as recommending 'a Gramscian approach to Canadian history'; Pâquet (2009) names Gramsci, with Fernande Roy (1988), as one of the prospectus's two explicit influences; Palmer (2009) argues that McKay's reading of Gramscian hegemony is too seamless, conflating hegemony and domination. McKay's own Gramscian outlook is drawn separately (gramsci → ian_mckay, revision 1.149). PhD context: 9 of the 91 PhDs citing McKay 2000 also cite a Gramsci work.
